task: round 12 skeptic (value + feasibility) of R12RT-5 (insertion-family successor guard for E10 v2)
reason: The gap is real, but the proposed remedy is aimed at the wrong step and its net value is about zero or negative. (1) The harm happens only at V4's PAIR step: the twin #38 is dropped and both finals carry an insertion. That step is not autonomous. The user re-ticks by 29 Sep 20:00 UTC (V4 text, CONTEXT 17:49 entry), so there are hours to read it. The proposed line instead blocks the autonomous PORT SUBMIT ('notify and wait, no autonomous port'). The submit is the time-critical step: ties go to the earlier submission, and round 11 valued an early port against doing nothing at +0.02..+0.26 P(bronze) given a successor. The user is asleep overnight (20:34Z directive), so the block can cost hours of tie order. (2) 'Forks > 62 on the 4 dummy clips' flags every successor that adds divisions, e.g. an ILP division-weight change, not only insertions. Division levers are a natural way to gain +0.001 over x138, so P(flag | successor) is likely 0.3-0.5 or more, not the 0.3 used for insertions only. 'A division-add stage in the diff' is a judgement call, not a mechanical rule. (3) Rough cost of the block: P(successor) 0.05-0.15 x P(flag) 0.3-0.5 x lost tie-order value ~0.03-0.08 P(bronze) = ~0.0005-0.006 P(bronze). That is the same order as, or larger than, the claimed benefit of 0.0005-0.002, so the net sign is unclear to negative. (4) The ladder finals draft has the same hole: reach0955/r_ladder.json L9 item 5 maps an adopted port to {PORT, V*}, where V* is K2 plus knobs and carries the insertion. The finding misses this. Checked and true: forks 62 -> 74 for the insertion on x138 (CONTEXT l.1517); HF v3 author CSV 62 forks, sha d52a5da2 == exp56; e10_port_gate.py l.859 already prints fork counts, so the classifier is free; E10 v2 is still PROPOSED with no OK, so a pre-trigger amendment is not post-hoc. The 20:33Z user decision ('one final for public, one for private') and L9 both still treat #38 as the insertion hedge. The hedge objection therefore matches the current plan; only the lever is wrong.
fix: Keep the autonomous port. Change only the PAIR rule, in the same pre-trigger v2 text before the user's OK and before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC. Proposed V4 line: 'If our port dummy CSV has > 62 forks on the 4 dummy clips (read from the e10_port_gate.py output), the port is insertion-family. Then the pair becomes {PORT, #38 56563534}, replacing #37, not {PORT, #37}, and V4's never-{PORT, #38} clause does not apply. Otherwise V4 as written.' Mirror it in ladder L9 item 5: for an insertion-family port the pair is {PORT, #38}, and V* does not enter. Record the fork count of both the author CSV and our dummy in e10_pull.json at the trigger. Everything else is unchanged: no mechanism, no code, R8 not touched, byte-identical N/A. It costs nothing in the no-successor world (~85-95%) and nothing in timing in the successor world.
realistic_gain: ~0.0005-0.002 P(bronze) (the finding's own arithmetic for the hedge), now with ~0 timing cost instead of a possible 0.0005-0.006 loss from blocking the port overnight. Zero in the ~85-95% no-successor world. It never touches the public score and leaves finals #37 + #38 unchanged unless a port is adopted.
